title: What the numbers in a profile mean
summary: Accuracy, best score, perfect rounds, top-10 rate and the performance index help you see a shooter's form, but they do not replace the results themselves.

body.html: A shooter profile on ClayArena shows several figures. They are calculated from the Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting competitions on the site, and the profile can show them for each discipline separately. They help you see a shooter's level and consistency at a glance.

Accuracy is the share of targets broken out of the targets shot at a competition. For example, 150 broken out of 200 is 75%. A profile can show the average accuracy across all of a shooter's finished competitions and the highest accuracy at a single competition.

Best score is the shooter's highest total at one competition. Compare totals only over the same number of targets. An international Sporting™ competition is 200 targets, shot in rounds of 25, while many club shoots have fewer targets. So if the number of targets differs, compare the accuracy instead. Accuracy lets you compare different numbers of targets, but layouts, weather and the level of the event still differ, so treat it as a rough guide.
A perfect round is a series with no miss. In the FITASC disciplines that means a round with all 25 targets broken. The profile counts how many such series a shooter has.

Top-10 rate is the share of competitions where the shooter finished in the top ten, in their category or overall. It also depends on who else is shooting: a top-ten place at a big international event is harder to reach than at a club shoot. A small category with only a few shooters makes the top ten easier to reach, too.

The performance index is one number that ClayArena works out from a shooter's results in one discipline. It lets you follow progress over time without reading each results table. It is not an official FITASC ranking.

You may also see other figures and sections, such as the match history, a view by season and a comparison with the winners. Their names may change as the site develops, so read the explanations on the site itself.

Numbers do not tell the whole story. Some layouts (sets of shooting stands and the targets thrown there) are easy and some are hard, and weather can change scores a lot. So the figures from one competition say little; figures over several competitions are more reliable.

For a beginner, a useful way to read a profile is to compare yourself with yourself: how your accuracy changed over the season. Comparing yourself with strong shooters can be interesting, but it says little about your own progress.

key_points.html: Accuracy is the share of targets broken out of the targets shot.
Compare totals only over the same number of targets; otherwise compare accuracy, as a rough guide.
Top-10 rate counts top-ten places in a category or overall, so it depends on how many shooters there were and how strong they were.
The performance index is a ClayArena figure, not a FITASC ranking.
Look at how the results change over several competitions.
